title: Rust test fixture can invoke the real system ssh (terminal_run_route_proxies_valid_remote_multibyte_commands) when its loopback health probe fails
outcome: No TermAl test can start a real ssh (or scp) process on any host, so full gates run without any risk of a real outbound SSH connection, as Greg's standing ban requires.
acceptance: Every test path that can reach RemoteConnection::start_process (or any other system ssh/scp invocation) uses an injected, non-network process starter or is otherwise proven unable to spawn a real ssh/scp, with a test that fails if a real ssh would be spawned.
terminal_run_route_proxies_valid_remote_multibyte_commands keeps its behavioural assertions, and a failed or timed-out /api/health probe in that fixture can no longer lead to a real ssh invocation.
Focused runs of the affected test modules pass on Linux and Windows, without retries or larger timeouts.
